subject.title: feat(memory-core): optional cross-encoder rerank stage for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw accept this MemoryRerankProvider SDK seam now, including the memoryRerankProviders manifest gate, exclusive single-slot behavior, and builtin-only scope?
rationale: The code path is plausible and well covered, but the change creates a new public plugin API and manifest contract whose shape cannot be safely decided by automation.

options.title: Approve The Seam After Rebase
options.body: Accept the SDK/manifest contract, require a current-main rebase that preserves memory_search cancellation, and rerun the memory-core/plugin-contract/docs/type checks before merge.

options.title: Revise The Contract
options.body: Keep the PR open but ask for a different gate, keyed provider registry, QMD parity plan, or narrower SDK surface before merging.

options.title: Park Or Reject Direction
options.body: Leave the PR behind the RFC or close it if maintainers decide remote/reranker support should use a different plugin or ClawHub-owned shape.

recommendation.title: Approve The Seam After Rebase
recommendation.body: Accept the SDK/manifest contract, require a current-main rebase that preserves memory_search cancellation, and rerun the memory-core/plugin-contract/docs/type checks before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is primarily plugin SDK and memory-boundary product/API direction, and steipete is the strongest available routing signal for those surfaces.
